children: Personnel of ground-handling agency AISATS are under scrutiny in the ongoing investigation into the immigration lapse involving three Italian nationals who travelled from Amritsar via Delhi to Munich without mandatory departure immigration clearance, sources told businessline.
As per sources, these personnel were responsible for guiding domestic and international passengers to the designated arrival exits or transfer gates, as applicable.
They have been suspended pending the investigation, another industry insider said.
When contacted, the ground-handling agency, a joint venture between Air India and SATS, did not respond to queries from businessline.
Meanwhile, authorities have initiated a review of existing procedures to strengthen the security mechanism for hub-and-spoke operations.

The development follows a show-cause notice issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) to Air India on September 12 over what it termed a “serious security and immigration-related lapse”. The Centre had also summoned the airline’s Chief Executive Officer, sources said.
According to the notice, three Italian nationals arrived at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport at 0050 hours on September 4 on Air India flight AI-1115 from Amritsar.
They subsequently travelled from Delhi to Munich on Lufthansa flight LH-763 at 0145 hours without obtaining mandatory departure immigration clearance.
Besides, the notice said the incident involved a violation of the prescribed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for hub-and-spoke operations.
On Monday, sources told businessline that an initial report and information indicated lapses in the ground-handling process.
Furthermore, sources familiar with the initial report said the passengers’ boarding cards carried a “D” marking, identifying them as domestic passengers on the Amritsar–Delhi leg.
Accordingly, they should have been directed through domestic arrivals and then proceeded to international departures to complete immigration formalities before boarding their onward flight.
However, sources said the passengers were allegedly routed through the international-to-international (I2I) transfer process instead of the domestic-to-international (D2I) process.
This allowed them direct access to the Lufthansa counter for their onward journey, bypassing departure immigration checks.
In July, MoCA launched hub-and-spoke international flight operations from Amritsar, making it the second spoke airport under the framework after Varanasi.
Under the facility, eligible passengers travelling overseas can complete check-in and departure immigration formalities at Amritsar before taking a connecting flight through Delhi.
Those who have completed immigration at Amritsar can use the I2I transfer facility at Delhi for their onward journey.
Air India’s AI-1115 was among the two daily flights designated for the airline’s ‘Easy Connect’ services from Amritsar.

title: AISATS personnel under scanner over Air India hub-and-spoke immigration lapse
